chung.Syllabus Name: Practice of Embedded System _Thực hành hệ thống nhúng
chung.Description:
- This practical module emphasizes hands-on experience with embedded systems by assembling, wiring, and interfacing hardware components with microcontroller boards. Students will practice programming and operating electrical, electronic, and microcontroller devices, reinforcing the theoretical knowledge acquired from embedded system modules. Through guided lab sessions, learners will configure and test peripherals such as GPIO, ADC, timers, communication interfaces (SPI, I2C, UART), and integrate them into functional applications.

- The course highlights real-world practices, including debugging, measurement, documentation of experiments, and the use of development tools such as S32 Design Studio and SDK. By the end of the module, students will gain practical skills in setting up embedded systems, verifying their operation, and applying learned theories to build and demonstrate complete embedded applications.
chung.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of lab sessions to be eligible for final assessment.

- Prepare before each lab by reviewing related theories and instructions provided by the instructor.

- Complete all assigned lab tasks, exercises, and reports on time, both individually and in groups.

- Use laptops, development boards, and lab equipment strictly for learning and project purposes.

- Maintain a lab notebook documenting circuit assembly, wiring diagrams, code, measurements, and observations.

- Actively participate in assembling, connecting, and programming microcontroller-based systems, testing functionality of peripherals (GPIO, ADC, timers, SPI, I2C, UART).

- Collaborate in team-based lab projects, demonstrating the integration of hardware and software into a complete embedded system.

- Apply theories from embedded system courses into practice, and seek feedback from instructors to improve performance and understanding.

- KIT S32K144(M4)

Module 1: Getting Started & GPIO (Slots 1–4)
M1-1. S32K144 EVB Introduction & Environment Setup
1.1. Introduction to S32K144 EVB board, ARM Cortex-M4 architecture, SDK, and S32 Design Studio tools.
Slide, Reference manual, Course syllabus, LAB Guide file.
1.2. Create and build the first project, flash the program, verify board connectivity.
Slide, Reference manual, Course syllabus, LAB Guide file.
1.3. Observe GPIO registers, study S32K144.h header structure, and run the LED sample code.
Slide, Reference manual, Course syllabus, LAB Guide file.

M1-2. GPIO Initialization & Output Control
2.1. Theory of PCC, PCR, PDDR, PSOR, and PCOR registers.
Slide, Reference manual, Course syllabus, LAB Guide file.
2.2. Lab 1.1–1.2: Implement Init_GPIO() and Set_GPIO() functions.
Slide, Reference manual, Course syllabus, LAB Guide file.
2.3. Debug and verify MUX, PDD, and PTSO bits in peripheral registers.

M1-3. GPIO Clear & Operator Design
3.1. Lab 1.3: Implement Clear_GPIO() using PCOR register operations.

3.2. Lab 1.4: Develop GPIO_OperatorInit, Register, Start, Reset functions.

3.3. Use a logic analyzer to monitor control and operator pin signals.
